title: Accessibility statement linked
question: Does the store link an accessibility statement?
method: Found when the home page links a page whose label or path names accessibility in the page language (accessibility, Barrierefreiheit, accessibilité, accesibilidad, acessibilidade, toegankelijkheid, accessibilità) or, for Brazil, shows the accessibility symbol; not found otherwise. Microenterprises are exempt from the European Accessibility Act, which the scan cannot tell.

spec.title: European Accessibility Act, Directive (EU) 2019/882, Article 13 and Annex V

title: Static accessibility basics
question: Do the pages read pass the accessibility basics that can be checked without rendering?
method: On the home page and sampled product pages: the html element declares a language, the page has a title, content images have alt text (empty alt for decoration is fine), form controls have a label or an accessible name, links and buttons have an accessible name, and the viewport does not disable zoom (user-scalable=no or maximum-scale below 2). Found when every page passes; review when some items fail; not found when most fail. Automated checks find a minority of barriers; contrast, keyboard use and focus need a rendered page.

title: Accessibility overlay detected
question: Does the store rely on an accessibility overlay widget?
method: Review when the static HTML loads a known overlay (accessiBe, UserWay, AudioEye, EqualWeb, Max Access and the like); found (none detected) otherwise. An overlay does not make a site conformant; regulators and courts have said so.

spec.title: FTC: Final order requiring accessiBe to pay $1 million over deceptive WCAG compliance claims (April 2025)
